checks.source_as_cited: Armstrong 2003 thesis; Candea & Fox 2003 HotOS IX; Litzkow, Livny, Mutka 1988 Condor ICDCS
checks.note: All three exist with right authors/year/venue (Condor: ICDCS 8, 1988, pp.104-111, confirmed by search record). Armstrong (supervision trees) and Candea-Fox (crash-only) support the OTP/crash-only parts. The 1988 Condor paper is about scavenging idle workstations with checkpoint and migration; from the abstract it does not describe jobs declaring resources, quota admission, hard-limit kills or per-account charging. Those are later batch-system features, so the batch-system sentence is weakly supported by this source.
checks.correction: Cite Condor 1988 only for idle-resource scheduling and checkpoint/migrate; cite a batch scheduler (e.g. Condor ClassAds, Slurm, PBS) for declared resources, admission, quotas and accounting.

checks.source_as_cited: F. W. Harris 1913, How many parts to make at once, Factory
checks.note: Standard EOQ origin (Factory, The Magazine of Management 10(2)). Used my knowledge of the standard record and textbooks; I did not open the paper. Assumptions listed are the standard EOQ ones.

checks.source_as_cited: Young 1974, CACM
checks.note: Confirmed via search: CACM 17(9), pp.530-531, Sept 1974. Formula sqrt(2*delta*M) confirmed by a secondary summary. Poisson and C much smaller than M are the usual assumptions, not checked in the original text.

checks.source_as_cited: Denning 1968, The working set model for program behavior, CACM
checks.note: CACM 11(5), 323-333. Standard textbook result. Wording that the OS evicts one page at a time is a gloss, but harmless. Based on known record, not re-opened.

checks.source_as_cited: Denning 1968, Thrashing: its causes and prevention, AFIPS FJCC
checks.note: AFIPS FJCC 1968, vol. 33, pp. 915-922. Working-set-based load control is the paper's central proposal. 'No collapse' is a qualitative claim, not a formal guarantee. Based on known record.

checks.source_as_cited: Silberschatz, Galvin, Gagne, 2018, Operating System Concepts 10th ed., CPU scheduling
checks.note: 10th edition (Wiley, 2018) exists; exponential averaging tau(n+1)=alpha*t(n)+(1-alpha)*tau(n) for SJF is in the CPU scheduling chapter. Based on standard textbook knowledge.

checks.source_as_cited: IEEE Std 1003.1 (POSIX) getrlimit/setrlimit
checks.note: Interface exists. POSIX does not guarantee a signal at every soft limit: only some resources (CPU time gives SIGXCPU, file size gives SIGXFSZ, stack gives SIGSEGV); others (address space, open files) just make calls fail. Nor does it bound overrun by an enforcement interval. The guarantee as stated is an engineering gloss. Based on known specification.
checks.correction: Soft limit triggers resource-specific behaviour (SIGXCPU/SIGXFSZ or failing calls); the hard limit is a ceiling on raising the soft limit, not itself a termination. The one-interval bound is not in POSIX.

checks.source_as_cited: Standard embedded and OS practice; no single paper
checks.note: No source is cited, so there is nothing to check. Progress-kicked watchdogs are common practice but the claimed detection bound was not verified against any reference.

checks.source_as_cited: Lampson & Redell 1980, Experience with processes and monitors in Mesa, CACM
checks.note: CACM 23(2), 105-117. Mesa notify as a hint with while-loop re-check is the paper's point. Based on known record.

checks.source_as_cited: Armstrong 2003 thesis, KTH
checks.note: Thesis exists and covers supervision trees and restart-and-escalate. The specific MaxR/MaxT restart-intensity parameters are formalised in the OTP supervisor documentation; the thesis discusses restart limits more informally. Not re-opened.
checks.correction: Also cite the Erlang/OTP supervisor documentation for MaxR/MaxT.

checks.source_as_cited: Gray & Reuter 1993, Transaction Processing: Concepts and Techniques
checks.note: Morgan Kaufmann 1993; covers write-ahead logging and commit records. Atomic rename is an OS file-system idiom, not from this book. Based on known record.

checks.source_as_cited: Young 1974, CACM
checks.note: Same source as D3-01; confirmed by search. Minimises expected lost work plus checkpoint cost under Poisson-style failures.

checks.source_as_cited: Bishop & Dilger 1996, Checking for race conditions in file accesses, Computing Systems
checks.note: Confirmed via search: Computing Systems 9(2), 131-152, Spring 1996. The paper is about detecting time-of-check/time-of-use flaws in file accesses, not about O_EXCL as a lock primitive. It supports the point that check-then-act is a race, not that exclusive create gives exactly-one-winner (that is POSIX open semantics).
checks.correction: Cite POSIX open() O_CREAT|O_EXCL for the guarantee; use Bishop-Dilger for why check-then-act is unsafe.

checks.source_as_cited: Gray & Cheriton 1989, Leases, SOSP
checks.note: SOSP 1989 (12th), pp.202-210. Leases rely on bounded clock drift; expiry of a crashed holder's claim is the core idea. Based on known record.

checks.source_as_cited: Amdahl 1967, AFIPS Spring Joint Computer Conference
checks.note: Paper exists (AFIPS SJCC 30, pp.483-485). It makes the serial-fraction argument verbally; the closed form 1/(s+(1-s)/N) is the standard later formalisation, not printed in it. Based on known record.

checks.source_as_cited: Gunther 2007, Guerrilla Capacity Planning, Springer
checks.note: Springer 2007. USL with alpha (contention) and beta (coherency), peak N*=sqrt((1-alpha)/beta). It is an empirical fit model, not a proven bound. Based on known record.

checks.source_as_cited: Derived here; Harris 1913 and Young 1974
checks.note: The source honestly states there is no single source for the partitioning step; the two cited works support only the square-root cost structure. The analogy to cache blocking is not backed by them.

checks.source_as_cited: Smith 1982, Cache memories, ACM Computing Surveys
checks.note: ACM Computing Surveys 14(3), 473-530; surveys write-back and dirty bits. Based on known record.

checks.source_as_cited: Candea & Fox 2003, Crash-only software, HotOS IX
checks.note: HotOS IX, 2003. Core thesis: stop by crashing, start by recovery, state in dedicated stores. Based on known record.

checks.source_as_cited: W. E. Smith 1956, Various optimizers for single-stage production, Naval Research Logistics Quarterly
checks.note: Naval Research Logistics Quarterly 3(1-2), 59-66. WSPT optimality for total weighted completion time on one machine, no precedence. The value-per-token extension is flagged as heuristic. Based on known record.

result.overall: All cited sources exist with correct authors, years and venues. Search records confirmed Young 1974, Bishop and Dilger 1996 and Condor 1988. The rest were checked against my own knowledge of the standard record, not by opening them. Claims are weak in four places. (1) Condor 1988 does not describe declared resources, admission, quotas or accounting. (2) POSIX rlimit has no uniform signal-at-soft-limit rule and no overrun bound. (3) Bishop and Dilger is about TOCTTOU detection, not the exclusive-create lock guarantee. (4) The Amdahl closed form and the MaxR/MaxT parameters are later formalisations, not printed in the cited works. D3-06 cites no source, and D3-12 says openly that it has none. No page text asked me to do anything.
